The column contract validation uses an order-sensitive `join()` comparison. According to the general rules, order-insensitive checks (such as set-based membership and size validation) should be used instead of order-sensitive comparisons like `join()` when validating a complete set of expected elements.

```javascript
  const expectedSet = new Set(contract.columns);
  const selectedSet = new Set(selectedColumns);
  if (expectedSet.size !== selectedSet.size || !contract.columns.every(col => selectedSet.has(col))) {
```

body: Implemented in commit `cc230d3b8`: `stripSqlComments` now uses a scanner-based implementation that preserves single-quoted, double-quoted, and dollar-quoted content while removing actual line and block comments. Verification: focused static contract 19/19 passed; combined migration security contracts 109/109 passed; GitHub `Security and Study Views Contract` succeeded.

Implemented in commit `cc230d3b8`: `splitTopLevelList` now detects dollar-quote delimiters, remains inside the quoted body across commas, and exits only at the matching delimiter. Verification: focused static contract 19/19 passed; combined migration security contracts 109/109 passed; GitHub `Security and Study Views Contract` succeeded.

Implemented in commit `cc230d3b8`: `findTopLevelFrom` now handles dollar-quoted bodies, so `from` text inside a quoted literal cannot be mistaken for the top-level FROM clause. Verification: focused static contract 19/19 passed; combined migration security contracts 109/109 passed; GitHub `Security and Study Views Contract` succeeded.

Thanks. I am intentionally retaining the order-sensitive checks. This PR protects exact view column names AND order; column order is a compatibility contract, not an unordered set. Runtime `SELECT *`, schema consumers, and migration compatibility can depend on `attnum` order. The final PostgreSQL catalog test independently asserts exact order using `pg_attribute.attnum`, and replacement/mutation tests must treat reordering as contract drift. Therefore `selectedColumns.join(,) !== contract.columns.join(,)` and `expect(selectedViewColumns(...)).toEqual(contract.columns)` are the intended behavior. Verification: focused static contract 19/19 passed; combined migration security contracts 109/109 passed; GitHub `Security and Study Views Contract` succeeded.

Formatting correction for the exact expressions retained:

- `selectedColumns.join(',') !== contract.columns.join(',')`
- `expect(selectedViewColumns(...)).toEqual(contract.columns)`

Both remain intentionally order-sensitive for the exact ordered schema compatibility contract described above.
